memo.headline: Put next quarter's effort into usability: it carries the largest complaint load of any focus area, and ads interruptions is the top-ranked issue that sits inside it.
situation: Review complaints split across four focus areas; usability holds the largest share of complaints, followed by billing_support, then playback, with access the smallest.
The top-ranked issue overall, other.general_negative, is a catch-all about the app feeling worse after an update. It has no single focus area, so it cannot be assigned to a team directly.

Of the issues that map cleanly to a focus area, billing.premium_only_controls ranks second and usability.ads_interruptions ranks third by priority score. Access.login_failure has the highest mean severity of the five but the smallest volume.

top_issues.why_it_matters: Highest priority score at {C4}, driven by volume ({C1} complaints) rather than severity (mean {C3}). Customers tie it to recent updates, but the label is too broad to act on without further triage.
Second-ranked at {C8}, with {C5} complaints at mean severity {C7}. Customers describe basic controls such as choosing a song, playing the next track and skipping as locked behind Premium.
Third-ranked at {C12} with {C9} complaints at mean severity {C11}. Reviewers report ads every one or two songs, and one says they are uninstalling over it.
Fourth-ranked at {C16} with {C13} complaints at mean severity {C15}. Reviewers say music stops mid-track and does not resume, even on a strong connection.
Fifth-ranked at {C20} from {C17} complaints, but with the highest mean severity of the five ({C19}). Reviewers cannot log in and get a false no-internet error while other apps work.

recommendation.argument: Usability has the largest complaint load of the four areas, and its main named issue, usability.ads_interruptions, is the third-ranked issue overall at {C12} from {C9} complaints. Among the issues that map to a single team, it is the second-largest after billing.premium_only_controls ({C8}), and the quotes describe ad frequency specifically (ads after every one or two songs), which is a concrete, testable thing to change. Its mean severity ({C11}) is lower than playback or access, so the case rests on volume, not on how badly each user is hurt.

alternatives.case_for: billing.premium_only_controls is the second-ranked issue at {C8} with mean severity {C7}, higher than the ads issue. The billing_support area has the second-largest complaint load.
alternatives.why_not_now: The complaints are about which features sit behind Premium, which is a packaging and pricing decision rather than a defect, and the reviews give no evidence on how changing it would affect the free-to-paid relationship. Ads and the paywall are also entangled in the quotes, so the usability work can proceed and inform that decision.

alternatives.case_for: playback.stops_skips_glitches is a real defect with a clear symptom, music stopping midway on a good connection, and a mean severity ({C15}) well above the ads issue.
alternatives.why_not_now: Its volume is much smaller ({C13} complaints against {C9} for ads), and playback's overall complaint load is well below usability's.

alternatives.case_for: access.login_failure has the highest mean severity ({C19}), and the false no-internet error blocks users from the app entirely.
alternatives.why_not_now: It has the smallest volume ({C17} complaints) and the lowest priority score of the five ({C20}); access is the smallest area by complaint load. It is a good candidate for a targeted bug fix rather than a quarter-long focus.

limitations: Reviews are self-selected public text, so they over-represent people motivated to complain and are not a measure of the whole user base.
The top-ranked issue, other.general_negative, is a catch-all and could hide problems from several focus areas; it is not attributed to any of them here.
One record was quarantined and a share of labels are flagged for review, so classifications carry some error.
Priority score multiplies volume by severity, so a high-volume, low-severity issue can outrank a rarer but more damaging one, as login failure shows.
The data contain no revenue, churn or user counts, so this memo cannot size business impact.
